examFacts.answer: The ACS CCN1 assessment is the core domestic gas safety assessment of the Nationally Accredited Certification Scheme. Gas engineers in Great Britain who want to join Gas Safe Register show their competence by a recognised qualification or by passing CCN1 plus the appliance assessments they need at a UKAS-accredited certification body's assessment centre. Assessments combine practical tasks and theory, and certificates are renewed every five years. Tigertest covers the knowledge side: the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998, HSE L56, the unsafe situations procedure, combustion and carbon monoxide, ventilation, flues, tightness testing, meters and safety devices.

landing.studyHeading: How to Prepare for ACS CCN1
tips: Know the unsafe situations procedure cold
Learn the difference between Immediately Dangerous and At Risk, what you must do for each, and what you need the responsible person's permission for. A wrong call here matters more than any score.
Know who the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations put duties on: the installer, the landlord, the responsible person. Know what the L56 code says about competence, safety checks and records.
Know what complete and incomplete combustion produce, the signs of an appliance making carbon monoxide, and the symptoms and actions when CO is suspected.
Tigertest tracks your accuracy by topic. Aim for 90 percent on every practice test, then retrain your weakest topic.
landing.faqHeading: Gas Safe ACS (CCN1) Frequently Asked Questions
faqs: It is the core domestic natural gas safety assessment of the Nationally Accredited Certification Scheme. Passing it, with the appliance assessments for the work you do, gives a certificate of competence that Gas Safe Register accepts for registration.
Does this practice test cover the practical assessment?

No. It covers the knowledge side: the law, L56, the unsafe situations procedure, combustion, CO, ventilation, flues, tightness testing, meters and safety devices. Pipework, live testing and appliance work are assessed hands-on at the assessment centre.
What pass mark should I aim for?

The scheme does not publish a percentage for the theory papers. Tigertest uses 70% as a readiness line; aim well above it, because a single wrong call on an Immediately Dangerous situation matters more than a score.

The Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 as amended and HSE's L56 code of practice, IGEM/G/11 Edition 2 (with the 2022 and 2024 amendments), the CCN1 criteria Issue 20.1 and, for building rules, England's Approved Document J. Northern Ireland has its own regulations.
How often do gas engineers have to be reassessed?
ACS certificates are renewed every five years, through ACS reassessment or the Group Competency Scheme.
